why: Lead tooling, fast-tracked, today's version: a new `land.ts stack <top-pr>` command (pr/Stack.ts) lands a native stack through three new PullRequests methods (stack, mergeQueue, mergeStack). It runs arm's leak gate and ## New names check on each open layer, then refuses when more layers are open than the base branch's merge_queue max_entries_to_build, read from GET repos/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch}, naming both numbers; then one gh stack merge --squash --yes, after the gh layer reads each layer's head again and refuses if one moved. The cause: stack 1522's 4 layers entered a queue that builds 2; the queue squashed the bottom alone and dropped the rest (github/gh-stack#444, #601, #616). Stack.test.ts: 7 laws green. Plants, each run once and restored: size check off turns the stack-of-3 law red; leak gate off turns the leak law red; names check off turns the New names law red. Each turned only its own law red.
note: No real stack was merged: the gh stack merge call and the stacks and rules reads were checked by hand with gh api only (stack 1522 listed with 4 layers; main's merge_queue rule reads build 2, merge 3). gh stack merge has no head pin of its own, so a push between the re-read and the merge is still possible; the window is one process start. The stack command does not read ci-required as land.ts queue does; the queue runs it.
